reason: Replace false leakage-free partitioning with current and historical audit evidence.
old: To preserve independence between model development and evaluation, partitioning was performed at source-corpus level after annotation and \gls{QA}, but before augmentation or any other task-specific transformation. Each dataset was divided into fixed training, validation and test subsets in proportions of \textbf{80/10/10}, without class stratification, balancing or resampling, thereby retaining the naturally occurring class composition of each corpus. The \gls{MDWD} partition was generated once through Roboflow, while the \gls{MTSD} was partitioned deterministically using seed~42, with images sharing identical SHA-256 hashes constrained to the same subset to prevent byte-identical files from crossing partition boundaries. Once established, these source-image assignments were retained throughout the subsequent experiments, providing a consistent basis for training, model selection and final evaluation within each dataset.
new:
Fixed training, validation and test partitions with nominal proportions of \textbf{80/10/10} were used. For the \gls{MTSD}, partitioning followed annotation and \gls{QA} and preceded offline augmentation. The seed-42 procedure grouped byte-identical images by SHA-256 hash before assigning them to subsets, without class stratification. This produced 5,986 training, 749 validation and 747 test images. The assignments were retained across the detection and prompt-localisation experiments, although different photographs of the same physical asset were not explicitly grouped.

The current \gls{MDWD} source export contains 2,956 training, 369 validation and 369 test images. Its historical v20 experiment export contains 29,487 training images after offline augmentation, together with 369 validation and 369 test images. The later source export is used for dataset characterisation; the historical export defines the recorded experiment inputs. The repository does not retain sufficient Roboflow version history to establish a completely unchanged annotation state between these exports.

An August 2026 source-mapping audit identified 17 source-file identities and 39 reviewed same-event groups spanning partitions in the historical \gls{MDWD} export. The same-event grouping affects 17 validation and 25 test images; 23 reviewed same-event pairs also cross partitions in the current source export. The \gls{MDWD} evaluation is therefore not event-independent. An earlier sensitivity analysis of four YOLO checkpoints, based on a different 30-stem filename heuristic, found changes of at most 0.48 percentage points in mAP after subset exclusion. That result applies only to the evaluated subsets and checkpoints and does not establish the effect of excluding all 39 subsequently identified event groups.

reason: Tourist Sign remains in training and broad prompts; evaluator filters categories, not spatial ignore regions.
old: A further distinction between the source and experiment-ready \gls{MTSD} taxonomies concerns the \emph{Tourist Sign} class. Only 33 instances were present in the source corpus, comprising 27 training, three validation and three test examples, which was considered insufficient for meaningful supervised learning or reliable class-specific evaluation given the visual variability of the category. Its annotations were therefore excluded from the experiment-ready target taxonomy used for supervised detection and zero-shot localisation. The corresponding bounding boxes were retained as ignore regions during localisation evaluation, such that predictions overlapping a Tourist Sign instance were excluded from true-positive and false-positive assignment rather than treated as background errors. This ensured that the class was neither learned nor evaluated as a modelled category while preventing valid localisation of an otherwise recognisable traffic sign from being penalised.
new: The \emph{Tourist Sign} category contains only 33 source instances: 27 training, three validation and three test examples. All twelve categories remain in the prepared training datasets. For the consolidated supervised evaluation, Tourist Sign is excluded from the reported category set by filtering its ground-truth annotations and predictions assigned to that category. This is a reporting exclusion, not removal from training or a spatial ignore-region mechanism; predictions assigned to another retained category are not exempted merely because they overlap a Tourist Sign. Prompt-based evaluation retains the full twelve-class source taxonomy, including Tourist Sign under the broad queries. These differences must be respected when comparing the experimental tracks.
